history.summary: This is the famous modern Shri Ram Mandir on VIP Road, Telibandha (opposite Hotel Babylon / Vishal Nagar), documented here as the CSV's 'Shri Ram Mandir, Raipur'. Built at a cost of about Rs 15 crore over ~5 years, the 105-108 ft high temple was crafted by artisans from Rajasthan and Odisha in Rajwada art style, with many Vishnu avatars carved on inner and outer walls. The Ram Lala idol is carved from a single Makrana marble stone that took 1.5 years to source and 4 months to carve; the rare sitting-posture Rama-Sita idols were carved by Jaipur artisans, and 5 kg of gold was used on the sanctum frame. The complex has 16 deity idols (Rama, Sita, Hanuman and others), a Navagraha temple and yagyashala near the entrance, a 500-seat hall, and a large 12-ft chandelier. AMBIGUITY (verify referent): Raipur also has the older Shri Ram Mandir Jaitusav Math ('Naya Mandir', built 1877 by the wife of freedom fighter Jaitu Sav, Purani Basti, where Gandhi once stayed) — if the CSV intends that historic math, this file covers the wrong temple.

name: Shri Ram Mandir, Raipur
town_description: Raipur is the capital of Chhattisgarh (since the state's formation in 2000) and its largest city, a major commercial and industrial hub of central India known for steel plants and rice milling. The old city around Purani Basti and the Kharun river preserves its pre-modern core, while newer areas like VIP Road and Naya Raipur reflect rapid recent growth. It is well connected by rail and air and serves as the gateway to Chhattisgarh's temples and national parks.

travel.road: VIP Road, Telibandha (opposite Hotel Babylon); well connected by city roads, parking can be difficult at peak hours
